page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-96 is a compute-optimized server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system operates at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 192 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core processing and memory bandwidth capabilities. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 21998.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 82913.7, placing it in the top tiers for raw computational throughput. It demonstrates high efficiency in text processing, image processing, and cryptographic operations, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU encryption score of 86639.74. Multi-threaded decompression via bzip3 reached 541.77 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput peaked at 129.97 GB/sec.

The c4-highcpu-96 offers high resource density for compute-heavy workloads, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. However, the low memory allocation of 2 GB per vCPU and the complete absence of local NVMe storage represent significant architectural tradeoffs. Workloads requiring large-scale in-memory databases or high-speed local disk caching will need to rely on network-attached storage or alternative instance families.

This instance is suited for compute-intensive tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, web serving, and cryptographic processing. It also supports moderate machine learning tasks, demonstrating strong performance in LLM prompt processing, though text generation speeds remain average for larger models due to the lack of dedicated GPU acceleration.
